title: Slabbed metric ingestor with trace-hook orchestration
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a resilient, low-cost metric ingestion layer that groups inference KPIs into fixed-size 'slabs' at the edge, preserves causal linkage to traces, and routes condensed envelopes to Prometheus/OTel pipelines. Motivation: bursty inference traffic from Dedicated and Private tenants is causing high cardinality and cost in the central metrics cluster. A slabbed ingestor will amortize overhead, reduce label cardinality, and make tail-latency attribution tractable without sacrificing causal trace links for debugging.

Scope:
- Edge-side component (sidecar or lightweight daemon) that accumulates per-request KPI tuples into time/size slabs (configurable slab window).
- Attach durable trace anchors: the ingestor must retain a canonical span ID + sampling hint per slab so downstream trace linkage can reconstruct contributing requests.
- Export path modes: 1) condensed OTLP envelopes for central OTEL collector; 2) Prometheus exposition push for legacy pipelines.
- Backpressure and fail-open behavior: when exporter is unavailable, persist last N slabs to local spill; if disk pressure occurs, fall back to probabilistic sampling to preserve SLA.
- Tenant-aware shaping: per-tenant slab windows and cardinality caps controlled by config pushed from central config service.

Deliverables:
- Edge ingestor binary + container image, with config flags for slab window, memory cap, and trace-anchor behavior.
- OTel exporter plugin producing compressed envelope with trace_anchor metadata.
- Prometheus pushgateway-compatible adapter for teams that still rely on scrape flows.
- E2E tests simulating bursty inference patterns (KV cache warmup, spike in streaming tokens).
- Grafana dashboard prototype showing slab-level aggregate latency, error-rate, and trace-link coverage.

Success criteria:
- 30–60% reduction in central metric write amplification for simulated Dedicated tenant workloads.
- >= 95% of slabs include a valid trace_anchor when sampling rate >= 1%.
- No increase in 95th percentile end-to-end latency from request path (< 5ms additional overhead at edge under normal load).

Non-goals: full replacement of existing per-request telemetry for debugging; the slabbed ingestor focuses on cost + long-term SLO monitoring, not fine-grained per-request debugging for all traffic.

Risks & mitigations:
- Losing causal coverage when slabs aggregate many diverse requests -> mitigation: include exemplar-level headers for outlier detection, and a fast-path that forwards full records for requests marked high-priority.
- Local state growth during exporter outage -> mitigation: bounded spill disk usage + backpressure signaling to the runtime to throttle low-priority telemetry.

Open questions:
- Which trace ID semantics are required for downstream reconstructability (full trace vs. span anchor)? Proposal: span anchor (trace_id + representative_span_id) is sufficient for attribution while keeping envelope compact.
- Default slab window: 5s vs 1s for streaming-heavy workloads. Prefer 1s for interactive apps; make configurable per deployment class.

Notes & links:
- Design doc (private): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Slabbed+Metric+Ingestor+Design
- Proto sketch & OTLP envelope: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-example-protos
comments: 2025-02-13 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff meeting notes. Agreed to start with sidecar prototype for Dedicated nodes. Marco to spike with a Go binary that groups metrics into slabs and attaches trace_anchor metadata.

2025-02-18 - Marco Ruiz: Spike complete. Prototype groups up to 256 metric tuples per slab, emits OTLP compressed envelope. Disk spill implemented using boltdb; local tests show ~3% CPU overhead on c5.large. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingestor/pull/128

2025-02-22 - Anika Sharma (SRE): Raised concern about Prometheus push compatibility for our enterprise customers. Suggested adding a push adapter that exposes a /push endpoint and converts slab envelopes into a low-cardinality metric set.
2025-02-27 - Marco Ruiz: Implemented push adapter. Integration tests added for Prometheus remote_write and pushgateway flows. Observed 48% reduction in label cardinality for simulated workloads.
2025-03-01 - Product (Liam O'Connor): Requested per-tenant admin knobs surfaced in Console for slab window and preservation thresholds. Added to scope, depends on Console feature toggle work.

2025-03-04 - Security (Jin Park): Reviewed trace_anchor implementation. No PII in anchors; recommended documenting retention and ACLs. Marked security_review_required=false but requested retention config in repo.

2025-03-05 - Marco Ruiz: Running canary on staging Dedicated cluster with 10k rps generator. Initial metrics: 55% write amplification reduction, 98% trace_anchor coverage at 2% sampling. Noting a bug where high-cardinality label sets bypass slab caps; created follow-up ENG-710911 to enforce label whitelist.

2025-03-05 - Aisha Patel: Next steps: harden spill behavior for extended exporter outages, add telemetry for slab drop counts, and coordinate Console change for tenant controls. Targeting rollout to Controlled Preview by 2025-03-25.
